title: The festival broadcast reissue and Henri Renaud at Columbia
summary: Columbia is releasing the festival broadcast thanks to Henri Renaud, who also arranged Clarke's concert with Dexter Gordon and Pierre Michelot.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: : So we were just saying that that was broadcast.
Uh-huh.
: A French broadcast. And you were saying that Columbia Records is just bringing that record out now.
Yeah, they just bought the tape and I just received the money from the union, so I know.
(Laughter)
: Yeah.
That the record will be out.
: Fancy that.
And like I said, it's -- well, it's been 28 years, almost 30 years ago, and now they decided that that was a very good broadcast. It was a fantastic festival.
: I wouldn't even have thought of that.
Well, this new -- well, it's between two people. Now, there's the Paris representatives of Columbia,
he's a pianist.
What's his name?
Henri Renaud.
Yes.
And a very good friend of mine. So like he looks into things and finds out what is really worthwhile.
And it's the day of reissues.
Right. To exploit. So he does that.
Now, the President of Columbia is a jazz fan. His name is Bert Luneval (PHONETIC).
He's done all of Ellington's things, right from the -- straight.
Right.
It's not being done in the U.S.
Right.
But it's being done here.
Yeah, well that was through Henri Renaud. Who is a wonderful musician.
I see.

And he fell into this job. He was commentator on the Radio Monte Carlo, which Columbia has a tie-in somewhere there, you know, in this building. So by Henri, I guess -- I suppose -- looking, always looking for records and new issues and some things like that, he fell into Columbia. So then he's been working for Columbia. Now, he left
Radio Monte Carlo and he's been working for Columbia now, oh, it must be at least eight years now. And he's responsible for most all the reissues.
Is he really.
Yeah. And now he -- we just did a concert with Dexter Gordon, who is under contract with Columbia.
Yeah.

So Henri set it up so that I would be the drummer and that Pierre Michelot (PHONETIC) would be the bassist. So he said well, since Dexter is doing this concert at Espace Cardin, I would like for you to be the drummer and Pierre Michelot -- he's one of the best bass players in Europe, and French, to do this concert, so that I can have a good tape to send to Bert, to see if he'll make a record of it. Now, we just did this this Sunday past, you know.
Is Bert -- Blumenthal?
Uh-huh.
Yeah. Oh, that's splendid, isn't it?
So now Henri's going to push it, because --
What's -- how do you spell his last name?
R-e-n-o-u-d.
Oh, Renaud.
Uh-huh. Renaud.
I see.
So he's going to push it and --
Very good. Very good. Well, okay.
